title: Ed Gein: The Serial Killer's Serial Killer
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Ed Gein, the Plainfield, Wisconsin farmhand and grave robber whose crimes inspired films like Psycho, Deranged, and The Texas Chain Saw Massacre. They cover his domineering mother Augusta, his brother Henry's suspicious death, the murders of Mary Hogan and Bernice Warden, the discovery of the House of Horrors, his insanity plea and commitment at Central State Hospital, the burning of his farmhouse, the auction of his car and cauldron, and his death and burial in Plainfield. The episode closes with a listener mail about eyewitness identification after a bike theft.

segments.title: Opening banter and tour announcements
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with tour dates and ticket plugs, a content warning about the grisly subject, and a brief introduction to Ed Gein and the films he inspired.
topics: Stuff You Should Know live tour

segments.title: Gein's childhood and mother Augusta
segments.summary: Ed Gein's birth in 1906 in Wisconsin, his religiously zealous and abusive mother Augusta, the family's move from La Crosse to Plainfield, failed farming, and his bullied school years with his older brother Henry.

segments.title: Father's death, Henry's death, and mother's decline
segments.summary: After their father George died in 1940, Ed babysat and did odd jobs. Henry died in a brush fire in which bruising suggested asphyxiation, and Ed was suspected of killing him. Augusta had a stroke and Ed cared for her until she died about a year after Henry.

segments.title: Mother's shrine and town oddities
segments.summary: After his mother's death Ed boarded up her rooms and let the house decay. He read anatomy books, pornography, horror and Nazi literature, babysat local children, and was considered harmless. Mary Hogan, a bar owner, vanished after he had joked about her staying at his house.

segments.title: Murders of Mary Hogan and Bernice Warden
segments.summary: Gein shot Mary Hogan in December and took her to the farm. In November 1957 he shot hardware store owner Bernice Warden with a rifle, took the cash register, and left her body; her son Frank Warden found the trail of blood and the receipt for antifreeze, then found her hanging in the summer kitchen, field-dressed like a deer.

segments.title: House of Horrors discovery and grave robbing confession
segments.summary: Investigators found body parts and objects made from human remains in the house, including what appeared to be bones and skin, and women's faces. Gein said he robbed graves, including his mother's. A psychiatrist suggested he was trying to recreate his mother. Errol Morris and Werner Herzog's aborted grave-verification plan is mentioned.

segments.title: Trial, insanity plea, and commitment
segments.summary: Lawyer William Belter entered a not guilty by reason of insanity plea. Gein was found unfit, diagnosed with schizophrenia, and held at Central State Hospital for about ten years. He was later found guilty of Warden's murder but insane, and his 1974 release petition was denied.

segments.title: Farmhouse burning, car auction, and cauldron
segments.summary: Townspeople burned the House of Horrors in March, and the contents were auctioned. Bunny Gibbon bought Gein's car and exhibited it at sideshows before it vanished. A cauldron later surfaced, was displayed by Evelyn Mayer's family, and is now at Basin's Haunted Museum in Las Vegas.

segments.title: Pop culture legacy and death
segments.summary: Robert Bloch's novel Psycho and Hitchcock's film were partly based on Gein, as were Deranged (1974) and Toby Hooper's The Texas Chain Saw Massacre. Gein died of cancer and respiratory illness in 1984 at the hospital, and was buried in Plainfield beside his mother and brother; his stolen headstone was not replaced.

segments.title: Listener mail: eyewitness identification
segments.summary: A listener named Karen from Memphis describes spotting a man trying to steal a neighbor's bike and calling police; the suspect the police later brought back was not the thief, showing how hard eyewitness identification is.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank listeners, mention the website and email, and sign off.
